messages:
Sam (sales): Heads up — AWS Marketplace procurement oddity for the NovaHealth POC. They want to purchase via AWS but treasury insists on a Letter of Credit (LoC) instead of marketplace invoices. Need legal + finance guidance on whether we can accept LoC for a marketplace-backed POC and how to route signature/orderform. @Tara (legal) @Kevin (finance)

Tara (legal): Is the customer buying through AWS Marketplace or are they trying to use AWS for cloud + our direct orderform? If it truly goes through marketplace, payments usually flow through AWS; LoC that directs payment to us is messy. Why do they want LoC?

Sam (sales): They say their internal procurement won't accept any AWS invoices — procurement will only sign if a bank LoC references our orderform. Customer says: "we need the bank to guarantee payment to your entity, not AWS." Also they've flagged DPA/data residency (EU) reqs for POC.

Miguel (solutions): For the POC we can scope to eu-west-1 and use a dedicated instance or private pilot to keep data in EU. That may push this into a direct contract (non-marketplace). It also changes pricing — dedicated eval pool ~= +$3k/mo.

Kevin (finance): We can work with LoC in principle, but legal needs to approve the LoC language and the beneficiary. If we accept LoC, it effectively bypasses marketplace billing rules. @Tara: can legal approve a LoC that names "Redwood Inference LLC" as beneficiary when procurement says they're buying via AWS?

Tara (legal): Two paths: 1) Keep it strictly as AWS Marketplace subscription — easiest operationally; insist customer use AWS billing. 2) Move to a direct orderform + MSA where we can accept LoC/wire. For a short POC we can accept a timeboxed LoC (90 days) but need specific wording and escrow/credit protections. Also DPA redlines: require EU processing only clause, SCCs or EU Addendum, customer-managed KMS option, and explicit subprocessor list + audit rights. I'll draft redline.

Sam (sales): Customer wants POC to start next week. Quick question: can we do a 90d pilot on dedicated infra with LoC and then move to marketplace subscription afterwards? Also they asked for wet-ink on the LoI — can we avoid that? :grimacing:

DeployBot: Invoice/Procurement Bot: Marketplace purchases are flagged for manual review. Tagging #finance-ops for procurement exception review.

Kevin (finance): We might approve a 90-day LoC for a pilot if legal signs off and treasury gets collateral. We would require LoC to cover full pilot amount + admin fee. Wet-ink is a pain — we prefer digital signature, but if their procurement team insists we'll need Sales Ops to accept scan + bank confirmation.

Sam (sales): Here's the PO details the buyer sent:
```
PO:
Customer: NovaHealth Inc
PO#: NH-PO-2026-314
Amount: $18,000
Term: 90 days pilot
Payment: Letter of Credit via Bank of Commerce
Contact: procurement@novahealth.com
```

Tara (legal): Uploading initial DPA redline shortly. Key items I'll add: Data Processing Location = EU only; SCCs/EU Addendum clause; KMS support (customer-managed where possible); subprocessor list + 30-day notice for new subs; fallback language: if dedicated/private infra required, customer accepts additional fees and revised orderform. Also require LoC language to reference the signed orderform and our legal entity.

Miguel (solutions): For the pilot we can provision eu-west-1 capacity and give them a dedicated slot. If we need to waive the setup fee, sales/finance needs to ok it. Estimated pilot incremental cost = $3,200/mo.

Kevin (finance): Finance can waive setup fee if LoC covers pilot amount + $500 admin. Need treasury confirmation; I'll ping them now.

Sam (sales): Action items: @Tara to post the DPA/MSA redline in this thread (ETA 4h); @Kevin to confirm treasury OK with LoC for 90d pilot; @Miguel to confirm capacity and provisional pricing; I'll ask the customer why they can't accept AWS invoices and push for marketplace route as default. I'll also ask if scanned signature + bank confirmation would work in lieu of wet-ink. ETA: EOD. :pray:

Tara (legal): Will do. Also recommend that Sales include a clause in the orderform: "Pilot is time-limited and automatically terminates unless converted to marketplace subscription or direct orderform within 90 days" to limit exposure.

Sam (sales): Perfect. Thanks everyone — will update after procurement call later today.
